newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Hagemeyer turnover and profits surge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hagemeyer turnover and profits surge.

text.p: Dutch trading group Hagemeyer NV said on Wednesday its 1996 turnover and profits rose sharply, boosted by the consolidation of former rival Borsumij Wehry, which it bought in 1995.
Net profit surged 47.5 percent to 285.2 million guilders ($151.8 million) in 1996, with turnover up by 43.6 percent to 8.22 billion guilders.
The group, in which Hong Kong's First Pacific Co has a controlling stake, said it expected profits and earnings per share to show a further increase in 1997.
Hagemeyer will pay a dividend of 2.28 guilders per share for last year and plans a two-for-one share split. Its shares closed 2.60 guilders higher at 165.50 apiece in Amsterdam.
The group said that organic growth of 4.6 percent fell short of expectations last year but it completed a number of smaller acquisitions.
Chairman Andrew Land told a news conference the group's earlier fears on a downturn in consumer electronics had been confirmed.
"Turnover from consumer electronics will probably be less than six percent of total 1997 turnover, compared to 31 percent in 1993."
But he was more upbeat on future growth, saying he expected an increase in turnover to 11 to 12 billion guilders within the next few years.
"We're aiming for an increase of 12 to 15 percent annually, partly through acquisitions," Land said, adding that half the growth would be organic and the remainder through takeovers.
